scope.caveat: Aetna, Cigna and UnitedHealthcare publish national commercial lists with no New York version; Oxford's list covers its own plans; Anthem posts no code-level list for New York commercial plans, so its answers depend on whether the member's plan uses Carelon. Individual self-funded groups can differ from every rule here.
scope.indications: Each rule records a policy's main indications, not all of them. A situation missing from a rule is not thereby uncovered.
scope.state_mandates: Not recorded. New York law requires insured group policies to cover a baseline mammogram at ages 35-39 and a yearly one from age 40, with no upper age limit (N.Y. Insurance Law section 3221); it does not bind self-funded plans. The age bands in this file are the payers' own.

code_selection.method: Top 12 advanced imaging codes (CT, MRI, nuclear, PET) and top 8 other diagnostic imaging codes by 2024 Medicare services in New York, CPT 70000-79999, radiation-therapy codes dropped. Medicare volume stands in for commercial volume.

meta.dx_matching: A dx entry is one ICD-10-CM code matched by prefix, or an inclusive range 'A-B' compared as text (so M48.00-M48.08 includes M48.061). Codes place a claim in an indication; the criteria decide coverage. Mapped codes were checked against the FY2027 ICD-10-CM code set.

criteria.prior_treatment: Provider-directed treatment, 6 weeks, started after the current symptoms or exam findings began or changed, failed; then clinical re-evaluation

indications.label: Red-flag presentation
indications.summary: Documented red flag, any of: motor weakness; cauda equina syndrome; suspected spinal cancer; suspected spinal infection; suspected fracture; severe radicular pain; each as defined in the criteria. Waives: the 6-week treatment trial. Imaging of the symptomatic spinal level only. Not a reason for spine imaging: known abdominal aortic aneurysm with new back or abdominal pain, or suspected acute dissection.

other: In-person clinical evaluation, with a neurological exam, for the current episode
Motor weakness, any of: new weakness of grade <=3/5 in specified muscles; new foot drop; new bilateral leg weakness; progressive motor, sensory or reflex deficits on re-evaluation
Cauda equina syndrome, any of: acute bilateral sciatica; saddle anesthesia; reduced anal sphincter tone; new bowel or bladder incontinence; otherwise unexplained acute urinary retention

Suspected spinal cancer, with any of: night pain; uncontrolled or unintended weight loss; pain unrelieved by change in position; age >70; severe or worsening spinal pain. With a known history of cancer, the oncology guideline (ONC-31.6) applies

Suspected spinal infection, with any of: fever; IV drug use; recent bacterial infection; recent spinal intervention; immunocompromised state; long-term systemic glucocorticoids; transplant recipient on anti-rejection medication; diabetes; HIV/AIDS; chronic dialysis; immunosuppressant therapy; neoplastic involvement of the spine; laboratory values indicating infection; decubitus ulcer or wound over the spine; X-ray or CT suspicious for infection; new neurologic deficit; cauda equina syndrome
Suspected fracture, pathological or after trauma: after an X-ray. Exception: no X-ray needed with ankylosing spondylitis or diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis

Severe radicular pain, all of: pain >=9/10 in a specified nerve-root distribution; significant functional loss at work or home; unresponsive to >=7 days of provider-directed treatment; plan for an epidural steroid injection, urgent spinal surgery or urgent spine-specialist referral

review.notes: CPB 0236 and the EviCore guideline differ (4- vs 6-week pathways; low back pain without neurological findings) and no document says which prevails. The CPB prints one pooled ICD-10 table, so codes are matched to indications by each row's description; it prints the disc-radiculopathy range as 'M51.14 - M54.17', read here as M51.14-M51.17. The table covers every spine region, so only its lumbar and lumbosacral codes are recorded. indications.label: Red-flag presentation
indications.summary: Documented red flag, any of: motor weakness; cauda equina syndrome; suspected spinal cancer; suspected spinal infection; suspected fracture; severe radicular pain; each as defined in the criteria. Waives: the 6-week treatment trial. Imaging of the symptomatic spinal level only. Not a reason for spine imaging: known abdominal aortic aneurysm with new back or abdominal pain, or suspected acute dissection.

other: In-person clinical evaluation, with a neurological exam, for the current episode
Motor weakness, any of: new weakness of grade <=3/5 in specified muscles; new foot drop; new bilateral leg weakness; progressive motor, sensory or reflex deficits on re-evaluation
Cauda equina syndrome, any of: acute bilateral sciatica; saddle anesthesia; reduced anal sphincter tone; new bowel or bladder incontinence; otherwise unexplained acute urinary retention

Suspected spinal cancer, with any of: night pain; uncontrolled or unintended weight loss; pain unrelieved by change in position; age >70; severe or worsening spinal pain. With a known history of cancer, the oncology guideline (ONC-31.6) applies

Suspected spinal infection, with any of: fever; IV drug use; recent bacterial infection; recent spinal intervention; immunocompromised state; long-term systemic glucocorticoids; transplant recipient on anti-rejection medication; diabetes; HIV/AIDS; chronic dialysis; immunosuppressant therapy; neoplastic involvement of the spine; laboratory values indicating infection; decubitus ulcer or wound over the spine; X-ray or CT suspicious for infection; new neurologic deficit; cauda equina syndrome
Suspected fracture, pathological or after trauma: after an X-ray. Exception: no X-ray needed with ankylosing spondylitis or diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis

Severe radicular pain, all of: pain >=9/10 in a specified nerve-root distribution; significant functional loss at work or home; unresponsive to >=7 days of provider-directed treatment; plan for an epidural steroid injection, urgent spinal surgery or urgent spine-specialist referral

indications.label: Resolved or improving pain
